findings.description: All calls to the decorated function now share and clear a single statistics dict (wrapped_f.statistics). Previously each call got its own copy.statistics dict. Concurrent or nested/recursive calls will clear and interleave each other's stats.
findings.rationale: Trigger: the same decorated function is called from multiple threads or recursively. The second call runs stats.clear() and writes into the same dict, wiping the first call's attempt_number and idle_for counters. Result: wrong statistics and potentially corrupted retry bookkeeping. The code comment about avoiding overwrites of local contexts shows this was a deliberate prior design.

findings.description: The async wrapper shares one statistics dict across all concurrent invocations and clears it at the start of each call.
findings.rationale: Trigger: asyncio.gather of several calls to the same decorated coroutine. Each new call clears the shared dict while other calls are mid-retry. Their statistics (attempt_number, idle_for) are reset or mixed, which gives wrong results. Previously each call had an isolated dict.
